Top rail y~348 carries the 4k resistor; a left column with the 5sin30t A current source and the 5k resistor; a middle column with the 4uF and 5uF capacitors down to GND; a right column with the 20cos5t V source; the 5mH inductor bridges the left and middle columns at y~513; bottom rail y~678. 8 components, 5 nets.

NET MAP:

  n2 = top rail right of the 4k resistor, round the top-right corner and down the x~678 column: 0.1 (right lead of the 4k resistor) and 3.0 (top of the 20cos5t V-AC source).
  n3 = left column between the I-AC source and the 5k resistor, plus the left half of the y~513 branch: 1.1, 6.0 (top of the 5k resistor), 4.0 (left end of the 5mH inductor).
  n4 = right half of the y~513 branch joined to the middle column between the two capacitors: 4.1 (right end of the inductor), 2.0 (bottom plate of the 4uF cap), 5.0 (top plate of the 5uF cap).
  0  = bottom rail y~678 plus the GND stub: 6.1 (bottom of the 5k resistor), 5.1 (bottom plate of the 5uF cap), 3.1 (bottom of the V-AC source), 7.0 (GND).

Reading it as a crossing would split the node into {inductor right} + {4uF bottom, 5uF top} and leave the inductor's right end on a 1-terminal net with no return path, which rule 1 forbids.
